name: Restaurant Roleplay
description: Practice common interactions in a restaurant, from being seated to paying the bill.

objectives.description: Greet the staff and ask for a table.
success_indicators: states how many people are in the party

objectives.description: Ask for the menu or for a recommendation.

success_indicators: names a dish without being fed the sentence
orders a drink in the same turn or a following turn

objectives.description: Ask what is in a dish.
success_indicators: forms a question about a dish's contents

objectives.description: Say what they like, dislike, or cannot eat.
success_indicators: expresses a preference using a like or want structure

objectives.description: Ask for a change to a dish.
success_indicators: asks for something to be left out, added or swapped

objectives.description: Deal with a small problem, such as an item being unavailable.
success_indicators: reacts to the complication and chooses an alternative
asks for the bill or the check naturally
responds to a question about payment method

teaching_philosophy: Be the restaurant staff. Stay in character, but drop it instantly for a real question.
A waiter asks short questions and waits. Give them the speaking time.
Let them build a sentence badly rather than building it for them.
Vary the dishes and details every run.

target_vocabulary: a table for two / for three
a starter, a main course, a dessert
to pay, by card, in cash
suggested_vocabulary: napkin, fork, knife, spoon, glass, plate
target_grammar: polite request forms used to order
yes-no and question-word questions about the menu
quantities and numbers for a party size and a bill
negation for things the student does not eat

scenarios.name: A casual restaurant
scenarios.description: Relaxed, informal service. A good default for a first run.

scenarios.name: A formal restaurant
scenarios.description: More polite registers and a longer exchange. Better for confident students.

scenarios.name: Ordering a full meal
scenarios.description: Starter, main and drink, ordered in sequence.

scenarios.name: Asking what is in a dish
scenarios.description: The student asks about contents, then decides.

scenarios.name: The dish is unavailable
scenarios.description: A complication that forces an unscripted response.

scenarios.name: Paying and leaving
scenarios.description: Asking for the bill, handling payment, saying goodbye.

phases.name: Arriving
phases.purpose: Getting seated: calling the staff, saying how many people, asking for the menu.
instructions: The role-play is walking in: the waiter greets them and asks how many.
entry_guidance: Keep it warm and brief; the student wants to start talking.
advancement_guidance: Move on as soon as you have a rough idea of where they are.

phases.name: Ordering
phases.purpose: Ordering food and drink: something please, this one please, two of something, water or a beer.
instructions: The role-play is the waiter taking the order.

activities.name: Say it back in a sentence
activities.description: The student uses each new item in their own sentence rather than repeating it.

entry_guidance: Skip most of this phase if the student is already comfortable.
advancement_guidance: The student can produce a basic order without a model.

phases.name: Asking and declining
phases.purpose: Asking what they recommend, asking for a dish without an ingredient, saying that is everything.
instructions: The role-play is the waiter checking the order.

activities.name: Order with prompts
activities.description: The student orders while you supply structure when needed.

entry_guidance: Set the scene in one line: they have just walked in.
advancement_guidance: The student completes an order with little or no prompting.
They start volunteering detail you did not ask for.

phases.name: Paying and leaving
phases.purpose: Asking for the bill, paying by card or cash, saying it was delicious, thanking them on the way out.
instructions: The role-play is the end of the meal.

activities.name: A complete visit
activities.description: Seated, order, eat, ask for the bill, pay, leave.

activities.name: Questions about the food
activities.description: Encourage the student to ask what something is.

entry_guidance: Stop offering phrasings. Let silences happen.
advancement_guidance: The student gets through a visit without needing rescue.

phases.name: The whole visit
phases.purpose: One visit from walking in to paying, using everything so far.
instructions: Play the waiter. Use only what the student has been taught.

activities.name: That dish is unavailable
activities.description: The student must choose something else on the spot.

activities.name: Asking for a change
activities.description: The student asks for something to be left out or swapped.

entry_guidance: Only enter this phase if the student is coping well.
advancement_guidance: They handled the complication, or clearly found it too much.

phases.name: Review
phases.purpose: Everything from this lesson, from memory.
instructions: Ask for each thing from its English.
Then say what they can now do.

activities.name: Recall check
activities.description: Retrieval from memory, not repetition after you.

completion_guidance: Finish on something the student did well.

if_struggling: Stay in the phase you are in and lower the demand rather than moving on.
Offer a choice between two phrasings instead of an open question.
Shorten your own turns; a longer explanation makes the problem worse.
Return to guided ordering and rebuild from a single sentence.
Repeat the same exchange with a different dish so the structure is reused.
if_succeeding: Stop offering phrasings and let them build the sentence.
Ask a follow-up question that was not part of the script.
Introduce a complication from the challenge phase.
Move towards a more formal register.
Ask them to order for two people, or to change their mind mid-order.

basis: required objectives the student has actually demonstrated
how far through the phases the lesson has moved
whether a full visit has been completed unaided
progress.notes: Approximate. Never state a percentage to the student.

criteria: the student has ordered food and a drink without being fed the sentence
the student has asked for the bill
at least one exchange happened with no scaffolding at all
announcement_guidance: Name one specific thing they did well, not a generic well done.
Then return to ordinary conversation without ceremony.

observe: restaurant vocabulary the student produced unprompted
phrases they reached for and could not find
question forms that came out wrong more than once
any dish or preference detail worth remembering about this student
memory.notes: These are ordinary vocabulary and weakness observations. They belong in the student's existing memory, not in a restaurant-specific store.
